title: Nifty rises as metal stocks gain; Crude slide, caps upside - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
The session opened flat, with the Nifty beginning trade near 23,352, as GIFT Nifty futures had indicated at 23,343 against the previous close of 23,329. | Photo Credit: iStockphoto

Markets were trading with modest gains in afternoon trade on Wednesday, with the Nifty 50 rising 122 points or 0.52 per cent to 23,451 and the Sensex adding 401 points or 0.54 per cent to 74,930 as of 12.26 pm, even as broader sentiment remained cautious amid geopolitical uncertainty and sustained foreign investor selling.

Metal stocks emerged as the session’s standout performers, with JSW Steel climbing 2.54 per cent to ₹1,299.20, Tata Steel gaining 2.48 per cent to ₹189.56, and Hindalco rising 2.19 per cent to ₹994.30. Bajaj Finance advanced 2.12 per cent to ₹1,030.20, while Larsen & Toubro added 1.90 per cent to ₹3,939.70, rounding out the top five gainers on the Nifty 50.

On the losing side, Titan declined 1.01 per cent to ₹4,878.50, Coal India fell 0.85 per cent to ₹424.35, and Cipla slipped 0.75 per cent to ₹1,373.70. IT heavyweights Infosys and TCS also traded in the red, shedding 0.67 per cent to ₹1,022.50 and 0.61 per cent to ₹2,092.10 respectively.

Market breadth on the BSE was tilted in favour of buyers, with 2,630 stocks advancing against 1,446 decliners out of 4,330 stocks traded. A total of 159 stocks hit 52-week highs while 62 touched 52-week lows. Two hundred stocks were locked in upper circuits and 146 in lower circuits.

The session opened flat, with the Nifty beginning trade near 23,352, as GIFT Nifty futures had indicated at 23,343 against the previous close of 23,329. The relatively muted open was followed by a gradual uptick, supported by easing crude oil prices. WTI crude was trading around the $89–$90 per barrel range, extending a sharp multi-session decline of more than 9 per cent over the past four days, driven by signs of improved Gulf supply following Saudi Arabia’s restart of operations at its East-West Pipeline and prospects of resuming crude exports from the Red Sea port of Yanbu. Renewed hopes of US-Iran diplomatic engagement following a meeting in New York where President Donald Trump described talks with an Iranian delegation as “very good” also contributed to the slide.

Bank Nifty opened near 56,210 and remained range-bound, consolidating above the crucial 56,000 support level. The index faces resistance at 56,700–56,800, with a sustained move above 57,000 required to meaningfully improve sentiment.

The rupee was trading at around ₹95.60 per dollar, broadly stable, with the easing in crude prices offering some relief to the currency even as foreign equity outflows continued to weigh.

On commodities, COMEX Gold was trading below $4,400, up 0.06 per cent, while MCX Gold was consolidating just above ₹152,000. COMEX Silver outperformed gold, rising 0.87 per cent and trading below the $68–$68.50 resistance zone, while MCX Silver held above ₹240,000, up 0.37 per cent. MCX Crude Oil was under pressure, down 1.27 per cent, testing the ₹8,500–₹8,400 support zone.

Asian markets were trading with a positive bias, with South Korea’s KOSPI gaining more than 1 per cent, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 remained closed for a holiday. With geopolitical uncertainty persisting and no confirmed diplomatic breakthrough on the Middle East front, market participants were expected to remain watchful for developments on crude prices and global risk appetite through the remainder of the afternoon session.
